blocks.text: Imagine navigating a city with roads that can change direction and even have tolls that can be negative. How do you find the shortest route?

blocks.markdown: In this unit, we will explore algorithms that find the shortest paths in graphs, even when edges have negative weights. We'll cover the Bellman-Ford algorithm, which can handle graphs with negative weight edges and detect negative cycles, and the Floyd-Warshall algorithm, which computes shortest paths between all pairs of vertices.

blocks.title: Shortest Path Problem
blocks.text: The shortest path problem involves finding the path between two vertices in a graph such that the sum of the weights of its constituent edges is minimized.

blocks.markdown:
### Bellman-Ford Algorithm
The Bellman-Ford algorithm finds the shortest paths from a single source vertex to all other vertices in a weighted graph. It is capable of handling graphs with negative weight edges and can also detect negative weight cycles.

blocks.title: Applying Bellman-Ford
blocks.prompt: Consider a graph with vertices A, B, C, and D, and edges with weights: A->B: 1, B->C: 2, A->C: 4, C->D: -1, D->B: -2. Use Bellman-Ford to find shortest paths from A.

steps.text: Initialize distances: d[A]=0, d[B]=∞, d[C]=∞, d[D]=∞.
Relax edges repeatedly for V-1 times (where V is the number of vertices).
After first iteration: d[B]=1, d[C]=3, d[D]=∞.
After second iteration: d[B]=1, d[C]=3, d[D]=2.
After third iteration: no change in distances, so final distances are: d[A]=0, d[B]=1, d[C]=3, d[D]=2.

blocks.answer: Shortest paths from A: d[A]=0, d[B]=1, d[C]=3, d[D]=2.

blocks.title: Negative Cycle Detection
blocks.text: If a graph contains a negative weight cycle reachable from the source, the Bellman-Ford algorithm will detect it by finding that a relaxation step can further reduce a distance after V-1 iterations.

blocks.markdown:
### Floyd-Warshall Algorithm
The Floyd-Warshall algorithm is used for finding shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in a graph. It uses a dynamic programming approach to iteratively improve the path estimates.

blocks.title: Floyd-Warshall Example
blocks.prompt: Find the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in the graph with adjacency matrix: \[\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 & \infty & 7 \\ 8 & 0 & 2 & \infty \\ 5 & \infty & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & \infty & \infty & 0 \end{bmatrix}\]

steps.text: Initialize the distance matrix with the given adjacency matrix.
For each vertex k, update the distance matrix using the Floyd-Warshall update rule.
After processing k=1: update distances using paths through vertex 1.
After processing k=2: update distances using paths through vertex 2.
After processing k=3: update distances using paths through vertex 3.
After processing k=4: update distances using paths through vertex 4.

rows: $O(V^2)$ or $O(E + V \log V)$ with priority queue
blocks.caption: Comparison of Shortest Path Algorithms

blocks.title: Algorithm Choice
blocks.text: Choosing the right algorithm depends on the graph's properties. For graphs with negative weights, Bellman-Ford or Floyd-Warshall are appropriate, but for non-negative weights and single-source shortest paths, Dijkstra's is more efficient.

points: Bellman-Ford can handle negative weights and detect negative cycles.
Floyd-Warshall computes all-pairs shortest paths using dynamic programming.
Choose algorithms based on graph properties and required outputs.
